article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Mostly sativa
Genetics: Neville’s Haze × KC 606
Breeder: KC Brains
THC Content: 20%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: terpinolene, limonene , pinene
Primary Flavors: Classic Haze, citrus, pine, herbs
Flowering Time (Indoor): 6–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late September to mid-October
Indoor Yield: Up to 160 g per plant
Outdoor Yield: Up to 800 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Special Haze belongs to a small group of cannabis varieties created to solve one of the oldest problems associated with Haze genetics: the wait. Traditional Haze marijuana can deliver some of the most energetic and expansive effects in cannabis, but its tropical ancestry often brings towering plants and flowering periods that stretch well beyond what many indoor growers can accommodate. KC Brains approached the problem by crossing Neville’s Haze with KC 606, producing a mostly sativa plant intended to preserve recognizable Haze flavor and mental clarity while becoming substantially more practical in a European grow room.

KC Brains officially markets the cultivar as Haze Special, although Special Haze has also been used as an alternate name in older strain references. The breeder currently lists indoor flowering at 6–9 weeks, outdoor flowering at 8–11 weeks, indoor heights around 125–150 centimeters, and outdoor plants reaching roughly 225–250 centimeters. The strain also won the overall Dorset Weedcup in 2001, giving this relatively inexpensive Dutch seed line a legitimate competition history.
Genetics and Lineage

The documented cross is Neville’s Haze × KC 606. Neville’s Haze supplies the unmistakable sativa side of the equation. Its family tree is rooted heavily in Original Haze , with Northern Lights #5 used historically to make those tropical genetics somewhat more manageable. The resulting influence brings narrow foliage, vigorous vertical growth, incense-like Haze character, and a cerebral high capable of feeling energetic, creative, and unusually long lasting.

KC 606 is more mysterious. Unlike Neville’s Haze, its complete ancestry has not been publicly documented in a reliable breeder record. Genetic databases generally identify KC 606 as an older mostly indica line of unknown parentage that appears throughout numerous KC Brains hybrids, including Bahia Blackhead, Leda Uno, Cristal Limit, Sweet Dreams, and Haze Special itself. Rather than inventing a family tree, the safest description is that KC 606 serves as KC Brains’ compacting and stabilizing influence in the cross.

The combination is what makes Special Haze unusual. Neville’s Haze normally points toward extended flowering and extreme sativa structure, yet KC Brains currently gives this hybrid a dramatically shorter 6–9 week indoor range. Individual growers have occasionally encountered longer-flowering plants, so phenotype variation should be expected, but the breeding goal is clear: retain Haze character while improving speed, structure, and overall cultivation practicality.
Effects and Experience

Special Haze places most of its weight in the head rather than the body. The beginning is typically bright and alert, with thoughts becoming more active and surroundings taking on greater sensory definition. Conversation can become easier, music more absorbing, and repetitive tasks less tedious. Compared with heavily sedating weed, the cultivar has a distinctly forward-moving quality that makes it better suited to daytime or early-evening use for experienced consumers.

Mental clarity is one of the more interesting features of the strain. A recent documented grower of KC Brains Haze Special described increased concentration and energy without the racing-thought quality that can accompany some strong sativas. That does not mean every consumer will experience it identically. Larger servings can still produce the scattered attention, heightened sensory awareness, or nervous stimulation associated with potent Haze-derived cannabis.

Physical relaxation develops more quietly in the background. Rather than pinning the body down, it usually acts as a stabilizing counterweight to the cerebral high. This makes Special Haze markedly different from indica-dominant marijuana where bodily heaviness becomes the central event. For many consumers, the appeal is precisely that ability to feel noticeably high while remaining interested in doing something.
Medical Benefits

Special Haze has not been studied as an individual cultivar in controlled clinical research, so medical claims cannot be established from its strain name. Its energetic THC-dominant profile may nevertheless appeal to some medical cannabis consumers who prefer varieties associated with alertness rather than immediate sedation. Temporary fatigue, low motivation, and periods of low mood are among the circumstances in which consumers sometimes choose stimulating sativa-style weed.

The strain may be less suitable for people who are particularly sensitive to strong cerebral THC effects. Heightened thinking, dizziness, dry mouth, elevated heart rate, and anxiety are possible, especially with larger amounts. Someone seeking nighttime sedation may also find Special Haze less appropriate than a heavier indica-dominant cultivar.

Anyone using marijuana for a medical condition should evaluate the cannabinoid content of the specific flower rather than relying on generalized strain data. Secondary sellers sometimes list THC around 20%, but KC Brains itself does not currently provide a laboratory cannabinoid percentage on the official cultivar page.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Classic Haze character forms the center of Special Haze’s aroma. Expect a mixture of fresh herbs, dry spice, pine, citrus peel, and the slightly sharp botanical quality associated with older Dutch sativa hybrids. KC Brains itself describes the cultivar simply as having a special Haze taste, while current breeder-linked listings add fresh and spicy qualities.

Individual plants can add more unusual accents. Limited grower tasting data has identified lime, pear, pepper, hash, and cedarwood, while another modern grow documented pine and lime aromas from the flowers. These observations should be treated as phenotype examples rather than universal flavor specifications, but they illustrate the cultivar’s range.

No authoritative terpene panel exists for the original KC Brains line. Terpinolene, limonene, pinene, myrcene, and beta-caryophyllene would all be plausible in cannabis expressing Haze, citrus, pine, and spice characteristics, but exact dominance requires laboratory analysis of the individual harvest.
Growing Information

Special Haze was originally designed with indoor cultivation in mind, although KC Brains explicitly states that it performs well outdoors too. Indoors, the breeder currently lists plants around 125–150 centimeters tall with yields reaching approximately 160 grams per plant. Outdoor specimens can stretch to roughly 225–250 centimeters and potentially produce as much as 800 grams per plant in favorable conditions. These are breeder ceilings rather than guaranteed harvests, and environmental quality will determine how closely individual plants approach them.

Vertical control deserves attention because the Neville’s Haze influence encourages stretch. Topping during vegetative growth, low-stress training, or a screen can spread vigorous branches horizontally and prevent the highest tops from crowding indoor lights. Narrower foliage helps light penetrate deeper into the canopy than it would in many broad-leaf indica varieties, but removing poorly illuminated lower growth can still redirect resources toward productive flowering sites.

The official indoor flowering period is unusually short at 6–9 weeks, while outdoor bloom is listed at 8–11 weeks with harvest from late September through approximately mid-October. Some individual plants may run longer, particularly when they lean heavily toward Neville’s Haze. Outdoors, strong sunlight and a relatively dry early autumn provide the best conditions. Overall, the cultivar is manageable for intermediate growers who want genuine Haze influence without committing garden space to an extreme tropical flowering cycle.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Special Haze?

The KC Brains cultivar is Neville’s Haze × KC 606. KC Brains officially sells it under the name Haze Special, although Special Haze has also appeared as an alternate name in older cannabis references.
Is Special Haze a sativa or indica?

It is a mostly sativa hybrid. Its narrow-leaf growth, energetic cerebral effects, and pronounced Haze flavor reflect the Neville’s Haze side strongly, while KC 606 helps make the plant more compact and faster finishing.
What does Special Haze taste like?
The flavor centers on classic Haze, with pine, fresh herbs, citrus, spice, and pepper. Some plants may add lime, pear, cedarwood, hash, or light tropical-fruit notes.
How long does Special Haze take to flower?

KC Brains currently lists approximately 6–9 weeks indoors and 8–11 weeks outdoors. Outdoor harvest typically falls between late September and mid-October. Phenotypes leaning strongly toward Neville’s Haze may require additional time.
Has Special Haze won any cannabis awards?
Yes. KC Brains states that Haze Special won the overall Dorset Weedcup in 2001, a Dutch cannabis competition held in Dordrecht and attended by prominent figures from the Netherlands cannabis scene.
Final Thoughts on Special Haze

Special Haze represents a practical interpretation of one of cannabis breeding’s most demanding genetic families. Neville’s Haze supplies the cerebral energy, narrow-leaf architecture, and unmistakable spicy botanical character, while KC 606 helps transform those qualities into a marijuana plant with a much more manageable cultivation cycle. The finished weed retains enough Haze personality to appeal to sativa enthusiasts without automatically requiring months of additional flowering.

Its 2001 Dorset Weedcup victory also gives the cultivar more historical substance than its relatively low-profile modern reputation might suggest. For growers interested in classic KC Brains genetics, Special Haze offers an unusual combination of old-school flavor, clear energetic effects, substantial outdoor production, and surprisingly fast breeder-listed maturation. In a cannabis market where many modern “Haze” strains contain increasingly distant Haze ancestry, this Neville’s Haze × KC 606 hybrid remains a direct and distinctive expression of the Dutch sativa-breeding tradition.
